thread:
maya: heads up — control-plane requeue storm in eu-west1 started ~02:10 UTC after the GPU pool ramp. workqueue length for controller-manager spiked to 18k.

sam: any apiserver 5xxs?

maya: small spike in apiserver 500s for ~2m, but root looks like controller-manager requeues and etcd latency. etcd saw leader transfer and increased commit time (~45ms -> 220ms). nvme iowait on the nodes hosting the raft leader around the same time.

lee: logs?

maya: pasted small snippet: ```I0321 02:12:34 controller.go:789] Requeuing key default/ingress-xyz: error syncing, requeueing: timed out waiting for cache; requeue rate 5m```

sam: deploy-bot shows a scheduled gpu pool scale event at 02:05 that added 40 GPUs (burst). could that cause network congestion / disk pressure during attach?

maya: timeline aligns. when nodes attach GPUs they also move lots of metadata and kubelet churns, we saw many kubelet restarts on tenant nodes which increased apiserver watch churn and bumped etcd leader io.

ops-bot: autoscaler: added 4 nodes to eu-west1-gpu-pool-2 at 02:06 UTC (scale reason: scheduled burst).

lee: cost angle — this caused controllers to retry a ton of reconciles (CRDs like Ingress, TFJob) which retriggered webhook calls and status updates. lots of tokenized operations -> write amplification to etcd and more CPU on control-plane. we're incurring extra reserved GPU minutes + control-plane request costs.

maya: action items I propose: 1) pause the scheduled burst for next 24h while we root cause. 2) roll back the nvme firmware update on the candidate nodes (recent change). 3) increase controller-manager leader-election/queue backoff config as a short-term mitigation (reduce requeue flood).

sam: agree on pausing burst. i've paused the scheduled job: `kubectl annotate cronburst/scheduled-burst paused=true --overwrite`

lee: for (2) can infra confirm node firmware was rolled last week? cc @infra-oncall

maya: infra-oncall confirmed: firmware roll 03/15 applied to eu-west1-nvme-3. candidate leader lay on that rack.

sam: for (3) what flags? i can patch helm chart for controller-manager to increase --min-resync-period and adjust workqueue backoff.

maya: something like `--leader-elect-lease-duration=60s --leader-elect-renew-deadline=45s` and bump `--concurrent-reconciles` down for the heavy CRD controllers (ingress, tfjob) temporarily. also increase client-go rate limiter: QPS 20 -> 40? (or lower depending).

lee: be careful increasing QPS — that could amplify writes. prefer increasing backoff and lowering concurrent reconciles.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: controller-manager patch candidate -> canary rollout ready (0/3 patched).

maya: short-term: lower concurrent reconcilers for ingress-controller from 20 -> 5, tfjob-controller 10 -> 2. set backoff exponential base to 2s -> 10s.

sam: i'll open a PR with those changes and run a canary in eu-west1 control-plane (single replica).

lee: also recommend disabling scheduled GPU burst tomorrow morning until infra validates nvme and attach path.

maya: opened follow-up incidents ticket #INC-2024-042 with timeline and metrics (etcd commit latency, workqueue length, apiserver 5xx). linking dashboards.

sam: owner matrix: pause burst -> sam (done), controller-manager config PR -> sam, firmware rollback investigation -> infra-oncall, short-term canary patch rollout -> maya.

lee: long-term: consider staggered GPU attach (throttle attach parallelism) and attach-rate limits in provisioning service, plus moving critical leader candidates off recently-updated racks for 72h post-firmware.

maya: agreed. gonna keep monitoring. ping me if you see requeue > 5k. :eyes:

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2024-042 - controlplane requeue storm in eu-west1 — severity S2.
